currentControls.summary: Core project migration validates retained schemas and opens newer schemas as opaque clones read-only without overwriting them. The report remains deep-frozen across per-tab session metadata clones and the document snapshot. It derives a frozen subset containing only unavailable and unknown items, recomputes counts, and shows bounded display names, stable feature IDs, availability, and declared dispositions while the owning tab is active. Exact render jobs deduplicate without weakening subscriber-scoped cancellation.

The manifest review marker and payload digest detect inconsistent edits but do not authenticate independent human approval.

The production Web build generates separate install metadata for Soundscaper and Framescaper and one content-addressed application-shell inventory. The stable no-store root worker recomputes that identity, sequentially fetches only the allowlist, verifies every complete body before caching it, and writes readiness last. Failed installation removes only the candidate; activation requires readiness and claims clients before retiring older complete shell caches. Production HTTP(S) registration is nonblocking, while Electron, non-HTTP documents, and unsupported browsers are unchanged. The Web preferences expose an explicit FFmpeg runtime download; no runtime download occurs implicitly. Its strict boundary permits only the pinned production origin and content-addressed versioned release layout, bounds pointer bytes to 64 KiB, manifest bytes to 512 KiB, each file to 64 MiB, aggregate files to 65 MiB, and streamed chunks to 4 MiB, and verifies pointer-bound manifest and asset lengths and SHA-256 digests. For non-identity Content-Encoding, decoded stream bounds and digests remain authoritative while cached responses are normalized. CacheStorage transactions isolate candidates and copy complete files before active-state publication; cooperative same-origin Web Locks serialize each fresh-state commit and cleanup, same-release retries reuse a complete cache, and post-commit cleanup is best effort. The store revalidates exact cached body lengths and SHA-256 digests and retains one prior complete release. Only state-committed active and previous descriptors are eligible through the service worker, whose cached responses are streamed through exact byte-length and SHA-256 verification before completion. The editor prefers a ready installed release and otherwise keeps its pinned network fallback. Focused Node and Chromium workflows cover shell identity, failed install and activation retention, two-product offline reload, explicit download, encoded, altered, and partial runtime handling, serialized publication, previous-version recovery, committed-only serving, cached-body revalidation, and orphan denial.

residualRisks.exposure: The Web consumer resolves the no-store final pointer at the pinned production origin, verifies pointer-bound manifest and runtime lengths and SHA-256 digests under bounded decoded streaming, serializes cooperative CacheStorage publication with Web Locks, commits complete state last, revalidates cached bodies, serves only state-committed active or previous descriptors, and retains one prior complete release.
